maren_held_early: ^A Grey Sister stands in the harbour office's doorway with a boathook held across it. A drowned sailor is on the step in front of her. She says a name to it, and it stops, and stands, and listens.
^"Sister Maren. That was a gunner. They stop for their names. Not for long."
^"The one who keeps them coming is out on the end of the mole, with his book. While he stands, they climb up. I'll go on naming them. I've more names than he has berths, I hope."

b: ^A Grey Sister sits in the harbour office's doorway with a boathook across her knees. On the mole outside, the drowned have lain down where they stood.
^Maren is sitting in the doorway now, the boathook across her knees. On the mole outside, the drowned have lain down where they stood.

maren_held: ^"Sister Maren, of the Quay Chapel. Hester sent you. She'll have charged you for the directions."

b: ^"Reedholm. You've the look. I was there too, copying names into the rolls. Now I say them out loud. It's a better use for them."
^"You're a cleric. Then you know the work is half prayer and half nerve. I've used up the nerve. The prayer is holding."
^"Mind that one by your boot. A cook. He'd mind being trodden on. He minded everything."

maren_ask: ^"I came out because they were coming in. Every night, up the quays, standing at the bollards. A name sends them back. It's all I have that works on them."
^"Someone stood on the lamp-stand at the end of the mole and sang them up. I heard it from the boat. He had a good voice. That was the worst of it."
^"You'll go after him. I'd like to come. The ones he wakes will want naming, and you'll be busy."

c-0: ^She stands, leans the boathook against the doorpost, thinks better of it, and takes it with her. On the way out she says one more name to the mole.
c-1: ^"Then I'll wait for the tide. They come up with it, and there should be a Sister here to meet them."

b: ^ "I'll walk at the back. If one of yours goes down, I'll get them up. If one of theirs does, I'll tell it who it was."
^ "No room. That's all right. I'll be at the Quay Chapel, saying names. Fetch me when you want me. I won't have finished."

s0: ^Maren is saying names under her breath. She finishes the one she's on before she looks up.
s1: ^"I'm listening. I can say names and listen at once. It's most of a chaplain's work."
s2: ^Maren falls into step, the boathook over her shoulder. She brought it back from the Mole. She says it has been more use than the psalter.

b: ^ "The quays are quiet at night now. Hester says it's the first thing on this coast she's had for nothing."
^ "Highmarch. I've been working out what to say to him. So far it's mostly names."
^ "He'll be on the Sol by now, in that coat. I said a prayer for him last night. It's the work. It doesn't mean I liked it."

maren_greet_fallen: ^'s name once, quietly, the way she says the drowned's.
^"That isn't one I mean to learn. Take them to the Quay Chapel, or whatever shrine is nearest. Yours get up. Mine don't."
maren_topics: ^What did you hear on the Mole?
maren_names: ^"Bosun. Two gunners. The cook. The boy who ran the lines." She stops there. "The fleet's. The harbour kept a muster of every crew that berthed, and the Quay Chapel had the copy. I read it until I knew it by heart."
^"The Sisters wrote names down for the empire once. I say them out loud instead. It's the same list. I'd like to think it's a different use."
maren_song: ^"A man on the lamp-stand at the mole's end, at night, singing. Not a quay song. It was older than the quays."
^"The drowned stood up when he sang, the whole fleet of them, and turned toward the land. Then he stopped singing. They didn't stop walking."
^"I'd like to tell him he has a good voice. Then I'd like to put him in the harbour with the boathook."
maren_hester: ^"Hester tolls everything: the chain, the gate, the quay, a question if you ask it twice. She has never once tolled the Chapel. She says she's waiting for it to turn a profit."
^"She'd have stopped me going out to the Mole. That's why I didn't ask."
maren_seventh_offer: ^Maren says names, one after another: the two League masters Hesk boarded, the gunner at the harbour office door, the boy who ran the lines. She stops when she has run out of the ones she means.
^"That's what he owes. The man who sang them up. He's in Highmarch, and the drowned came down that road from him, in step."
^"Hester's people say his walls are full of legionaries in the old harness, drilling for a coronation. He means to be crowned in the capital. I'd like a word with him before he goes."

^"I said I'd tell him he has a good voice. Hester has the League's say on Highmarch. Ask her at the Paid Toll, and I'll come up the road with you. I've even told her I'm going, in writing. It's a first."

s0: ^"Go on. I'll catch up. I've a name to finish."
s1: ^Maren has gone back to her names.
s2: ^"Mind the weed on the steps. It's had a long time to get slippery."
